[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, Digital Realty ACC9, matches a Baxtel listing and a datacenterHawk listing, both whose own building code exactly matches this rows name, giving 21745 Sir Timothy Drive, Ashburn, VA, part of the former DuPont Fabros Ashburn Corporate Campus this session traced to the September 2017 merger.

reading.body:
Digital Realty ACC9 is a named building within the operator's Northern Virginia campus in Ashburn, Virginia, one of the largest colocation facility concentrations in the US. The building's individual power capacity is not published. Digital Realty reports approximately 600 MW of IT load across its entire Loudoun County footprint as of 2023, but no figure breaks out ACC9's share of that total.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 have published power capacity totaling 1,375 MW. Digital Realty's Northern Virginia campus as a whole ranks 24th by published megawatts in the state. The building derives its ACC9 designation from the Ashburn Corporate Campus naming convention established by DuPont Fabros Technology before Digital Realty's acquisition of that operator in 2017.

Without a building-specific power figure, ACC9 cannot be assessed as a distinct constraint on AI scaling. Its relevance depends on whether the operator or the site's monitoring network publishes a capacity allocation for this address. The Northern Virginia region as a whole remains critical infrastructure for cloud and AI workloads, but individual facility figures remain opaque.
